rationale: PINS the RECOVERY BOUNDARY of GO-GAP-1, which is the real cost of the grammar pin and not the exotic syntax. Two constructs in this file are LEGAL Go and the PREVIOUSLY wired tree-sitter-go errored on both: a package-scope generic function VALUE (`var _ = Backward[[]int]`, Go 1.21+) and a method on an INSTANTIATED generic receiver (`func (Either[A, B]) Fst() A`, Go 1.18+). The damage was ERROR RECOVERY: everything after the first error was re-read as composite-literal debris, so declarations AFTER the error site stopped being declarations. MEASURED ON A REAL CORPUS FILE (go-tools/go/analysis/passes/modernize/testdata/src/slicesbackward/slicesbackward.go, which carries the same construct on line 11): the old wired build produced 1 symbol, 195 parse errors and 0 `contains` edges; the pinned build produces 40 symbols, 0 errors and 4 `contains`. 39 of that file's 40 declarations were being lost. THIS FIXTURE IS THEREFORE ABOUT THE DECLARATIONS, NOT THE SYNTAX: every expected row below is a fact about a declaration that sits AFTER an error site under the old grammar. THE FOUR EXPECTED-SYMBOL ROWS ARE THE PIN: `afterTheValue` (declared immediately after the generic VALUE) and `afterTheMethod` (declared after the instantiated-receiver method) must be `function` symbols, `Either` must be a `struct`, and `Fst` must be a `method` — a swallowing grammar loses all four silently, publishing neither symbols nor `contains`. THE THREE EDGE GROUPS PIN THE SAME THING FROM THE OTHER SIDE: `afterTheValue -> Lock @32` and `afterTheValue -> Unlock @33` are REAL CALLS inside a function the old grammar never saw as a function at all, so they could not have been attributed to it; `Either -> Fst @43` is the `contains` row that says the method on an instantiated generic receiver belongs to its type; `Fst -> Either @43` is the receiver reference back. WHY THE GRAMMAR IS A PIN BUMP AND NOT A PATCH: e395081 is an upstream commit, so the wired wasm is a stock build; the provenance and the full A/B are in grammars/tree-sitter-go/PIN.md. WHY THE ANALYZER CHANGE SHIPS WITH IT: the newer grammar types a generic CALL as `type_conversion_expression` over a `generic_type` instead of a `call_expression` with an `identifier` function, so the grammar alone would silence 140 corpus calls and 2 fixtures — the same commit teaches the call passes to read the new shape, and the type/call decision stays semantic (`isGoPackageCallable`), which is where Go puts it. NOT PINNED: `imports`, `exports` and the `references` rows into generic type parameters (`Slice`, `E`, `A`, `B`), which the declared-type pass owns unchanged; and the A/B cost, which is stated in PIN.md rather than asserted here.

expectRelationships.comment: A REAL CALL inside the function declared immediately after the package-scope generic VALUE. The old grammar never saw this as a function at all, so it could not attribute the call to it.
The second call in the same recovered function.
The method on an INSTANTIATED generic receiver belongs to its type — the `contains` row a swallowing grammar cannot produce.
The receiver reference back from the method on the instantiated generic receiver.

forbidRelationships.comment: The generic VALUE is not a call. `var _ = Backward[[]int]` names Backward as a value; the analyzer must not claim a call site at line 27.

An ERROR-region construct must not become a construction of a name the source never constructs. This is the identical class go/grammar-error-not-a-construction-889 pins, and the grammar bump must not reintroduce it.
